newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs $0.50-$1 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs $0.50-$1 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower amid light demand from packers still fighting soft operating margins, dealers said.
Plans for Saturday slaughter were extremely thin, with only a handful of packers expected to be open, they said.
Saturday's hog slaughter estimates ranged from 10,000 to 30,000 head against 26,000 a week ago and 12,000 a year ago.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold down $0.50 TO $1.00 AT $57.00 TO $59.00 in the country and $59.50 to $60.50 at plants, the dealers said.
Illinois hogs sold $1.00 lower at $58.00 to $59.50 in the country and $60.00 to $60.50 for hogs delivered to the plant.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $57.00 in the country and $60.00 at plants. Demand was extremely light.
Ohio hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower, with a top of $57.00 in the country and $58.00 at plants.
"It's the same old thing - poor demand," one Ohio hog buyer said.
Light slaughter the past several weeks continued to lend support to pork prices as thin to moderate pork demand buoyed values amid tight fresh pork stocks, market sources said.

Pork cut-out values Thursday were up $0.62 to $0.68 per cwt, with the U.S. Number Two carcass value up $0.64 at $79.52, compared with Wednesday and up $5.79 since May 5 when prices started climbing, USDA statistics showed.
